# Overview

`Edge_ORA()` performs miRNA gene interaction (MGI) enrichment analysis by
testing the overlap between a set of differentially expressed MGIs and
each pathway's MGI set. The pathway MGI set is generated by linking the
pathway gene set to `background_MGI`. This is an edge based method, and
unlike the `TG_` and `MiR_` methods it operates on miRNA to gene pairs
rather than miRNAs or genes alone. This is a standard over-representation
analysis, built on `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("clusterProfiler")`'s
`enricher()`.

This vignette uses the same toy BLCA example data as the package's main
Quick Start vignette. See `vignette("miREA")` for a description of that
data and for running all nine methods together through `miREA()`.

# Required inputs

* `pathway`, a two column data frame with columns `pathway` and `gene`.
* `mir_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `miRNA`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `gene_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `gene`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `mir_mat` and `gene_mat`, raw expression matrices with samples as
  columns, used to correlate miRNA and gene expression within the tumor
  samples and flag DEMGI pairs.
* `background_MGI`, a two column data frame with columns `miRNA` and
  `gene`, or `NULL` to use the bundled default (see `vignette("miREA")`,
  Step 1, for details on `background_MGI`).
* `background` for `Edge_ORA()` itself, a character vector of background
  MGIs formatted as `[miRNA]:[gene]`.

```{r load-data}
library(miREA)
data(toy_pathway)
data(toy_mir_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_mat)
data(toy_mir_mat)
data(background_MGI)
```

# Run Edge-ORA

```{r prepare-input}
input_data <- getAllInputData(
    methods = "Edge_ORA",
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata,
    gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI,
    gene_mat = toy_gene_mat,
    mir_mat = toy_mir_mat
)
```

`input_data$data$Edge_ORA` holds the differentially expressed MGIs, built
by `getAllInputData()` from correlating `toy_gene_mat` and `toy_mir_mat`
expression within the tumor samples. `input_data$pathway$Edge` holds the
pathway MGI sets, derived from `toy_pathway`'s genes through
`background_MGI`.

```{r run-edge-ora}
background <- unique(paste0(background_MGI$miRNA, ":", background_MGI$gene))
res <- Edge_ORA(
    DEMGI = input_data$data$Edge_ORA,
    background = background,
    pathway = input_data$pathway$Edge,
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
head(res)
```

# Run through miREA()

`Edge_ORA()` can also be run through the `miREA()` wrapper, which is
useful when you want its result alongside other methods' results in a
single `miREAResult` object (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 2, for the
multi-method case). For a single target, `background` can be a plain
character vector instead of a named list.

```{r run-through-miREA}
result <- miREA(
    methods = "Edge_ORA",
    input_data = input_data,
    background = background,
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
head(result$result$Edge_ORA)
```

# Supplying your own MGI list

If you already have a list of differentially expressed MGIs from an
external analysis instead of letting `getAllInputData()` derive one from
expression and differential expression data, call `Edge_ORA()` directly
with that list and `input_data$pathway$Edge`. `DEMGI` must be a character
vector formatted as `[miRNA]:[gene]`.

```{r custom-list, eval=FALSE}
# replace with your own MGI list
my_DEMGI <- c("hsa-miR-21-5p:TP53", "hsa-miR-155-5p:MYC")
res_custom <- Edge_ORA(
    DEMGI = my_DEMGI,
    background = background,
    pathway = input_data$pathway$Edge,
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
```
